To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the substitution of titanium and cobalt into the barium ferrite structure results in an increase in coercivity, which is due to the increase of the magnetocrystaline anisotopy field and the decrease of the magnetic moment.

the temperature dependence of the coercivity of (Ti,Co)Ba-ferrites differs from that of non-substituted material and that this difference can be explained in terms of a much steeper temperature dependence of the anisotropy and the possibility that the reversal mechanism changes from coherent to in-coherent. > The most interesting aspect of the results is the possibility to control the temperature dependence of coercive field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of barium ferrites with the general formula (Ba _{1-} x Ti _{x} )(Co _{1-} y )Fe _{12-y} O _{19}.
the magnetic and structural properties of the barium ferrite family.

the synthesis of (Ti, Co)substituted bar- ium ferrites, the investigation of their magnetic properties, and the interpretation of these properties in terms of the magnetocrystal- linic anisotropy, magnetization reversal mechanism, and magnetic domain structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic behavior of (Ti,Co)BaFe _{12} O _{19} is dominated by the competition of two different anisotropy fields.

the magnetic properties of (Ti, Co) substituted barium ferrite are very sensitive to the preparation method and the composition, which makes it very difficult to predict the properties of the material from the composition.

the substitution of Ti for Ba in barium ferrite leads to a decrease in coercivity with temperature which is less pronounced than that of the parent barium ferrite, but the decrease in coercivity is not as large as that observed in the corresponding strontium ferrite system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the substitution of Co for Fe3+ in barium hexaferrites leads to a decrease in magnetocrystallin anisotropy constant and a substantial decrease in coercive force at low temperatures.
the magnetic properties of barium ferrites can be tailored for a variety of applications by substituting the appropriate elements.
we have demonstrated the possibility of controlling the magnetic properties of barium hexaferrite by the substitution of Ti4+ for Ba2+ and Co2+ for Fe3+.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of Ti and Co substitution in barium ferrites can lead to a large increase of the coercivity, which is maintained at low temperatures and is accompanied by a large reduction of the magnetocrstalline anisotropic field.

the temperature dependence of coercive field is not a reliable indicator of magnetization reversal mechanism in ferrites, and the temperature dependence of magnetocrystallin anisotropy is a much more important factor.
the temperature dependence of coercive field is not universal and that the mechanism for the magnetization reversal can change as temperature is varied.
